Diego Alvarez: Produce lightweight test harness and latency spreadsheet for 512/2048 token profiles (due: 2026-03-12)

meeting_header: Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 16:00 PT | Duration: ~58 minutes | Redwood: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Noah Patel | Customer: Lena Park, Samir Rao, Priya Menon, Omar Aziz
summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage trajectory, burn rate concerns, and capacity planning for Q2. Northpoint noted a 48% month-over-month increase in inference volume driven by new clinical summarization feature. Finance flagged higher-than-expected variable spend. Redwood proposed a Dedicated sizing recommendation, batching/kv-cache suggestions, and a pilot for quantized model variants to control token cost while meeting p95 latency. Action items assigned and follow-up technical deep dive agreed.
topics: cost / burn rate and finance guardrails
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick status then dig into the numbers. Lena, you wanted to kick off with usage?

[00:28] Lena Park (Northpoint): Yeah hi, thanks. we've seen a big uptick since feb launch, roughly 48% mom in generation calls. peak windows are late afternoon EST, and the p95 is creeping up to about 420ms for the 512 token jobs.
[00:52] Samir Rao (Northpoint): To add, the clinical summaries are sensitive to latency; physicians complained about stutters. we're also seeing variation with long-context threads which pushes cost.

[01:20] Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE): okay that matches the telemetry we pulled. initial thought, two levers: move hot routes to Dedicated capacity and enable prefix KV caching for the multi-turn threads. that should drop per-token compute and p95.
[01:55] Omar Aziz (Northpoint SRE): Quick Q, how would failover work if Dedicated saturates? we need deterministic fallback behaviour for our SLAs.

[02:18] Noah Patel (Redwood CSM): We can configure smart routing — policy-based. default is dedicated-first, then hosted fallback to compatible smaller variants. we can show policy config in the runbook.
[02:38] Priya Menon (Finance): Sorry — can someone say what that means for spend? our burn this month was 2.6x planned. we need a ceiling and predictability.

[02:58] Maya Chen: Totally understood. the plan is to model committed Dedicated tiers vs variable hosted. we'll run a month-by-month forecast and show crossover points. also quantization/optimize suggestions could reduce unit spend by 20-40% on CPU-bound models.
[03:38] Lena: When you say quantization, are we talking 4-bit/8-bit? i'm worried about quality regressions for clinical outputs.

[03:52] Diego: Great point. we propose an evaluation harness with canary prompts. start with 8-bit post-training quant and compare ROUGE and hallucination rates on a dev prompt set. if pass, run a small production pilot.
[04:18] Samir: We also need SOC 2 audit details, and KMS integration. our security team will require SSO and log retention for six months.

[04:36] Maya: Redwood supports SAML/SSO, and our private deployments can integrate with KMS/HSM. retention and audit logs are configurable in the Console. i'll attach the security brief after the call.
[04:58] Priya: Perfect. finance wants a clear 'if X usage, then Y cost' table. chart please.
[05:12] Maya: we'll include cost bands in the forecast. two scenarios — conservative and aggressive growth. also show break-even for Dedicated commitment.
[05:40] Lena: latency targets — p95 350ms is our aim. is that realistic with Dedicated?

[05:56] Diego: Yes, on a dedicated 2-card A100-equivalent pool with batching tuned for your token distribution, p95 250-320ms is achievable. caveat: long context sessions will still be higher unless we KV-cache prefixes.
[06:30] Samir: what's the ops burden for Dedicated vs Hosted? our infra team prefers less operational overhead.

[06:45] Noah: Dedicated has more configuration up front but predictable throughput. Hosted is zero infra but variable performance and cost. Redwood Private (VPC) is middle ground with customer-managed network and our control plane.
[07:05] Omar: network egress and data residency — we must keep PHI inside region. can we pin instances to us-east-2?
[07:22] Diego: yes, region pinning supported. for Private on-prem we can do air-gapped in worst-case, but requires enterprise contract and timeline for deployment.
[07:48] Priya: timeline concern — if we commit to Dedicated, what's the lead time?
[08:00] Maya: Typically 2-4 weeks to provision and test for standard Dedicated pools, longer for Private/on-prem. we'll include timeline in the deliverable.
[08:24] Lena: i want to surface one incident — last Monday a model flip caused a 30% latency spike. need automatic fallback and better observability on model rollouts.
[08:42] Diego: Rollouts: canary + automatic rollback on latency regressions. the Console shows per-route latency and token cost; we can set alerts and automatic fallback to previous model.
[09:05] Samir: excellent. can the fallback pick a quantized variant if available? that might save cost while preserving throughput.
[09:18] Diego: yes, routing policies can prefer a quantized variant when p95 breaches or capacity thresholds hit.
[09:38] Priya: about the cost spike — was it expected because of a promo?
[09:46] Lena: no, it was organic traffic plus a bug in our client that retried aggressively. we've patched the client but want Guardrails from Redwood to prevent runaway spend.
[10:05] Maya: We'll set per-route quotas and auto-throttle policies; also show autoscaling caps on Dedicated pools. we'll include a recommended guardrail config in the runbook.
[10:40] [Speaker 1]: (inaudible) ...sorry, could you repeat recommended batch sizes?
[10:52] Diego: For 512 token median, batching 8-12 requests with continuous batching window of 20-40ms is a good start. we can tune live with load tests.
[11:10] Samir: we want an A/B: keep hosted for infrequent routes, Dedicated for high-throughput. what's the math?
[11:26] Maya: We'll model three classes: cold infrequent, warm mid, hot high-throughput. include token cost per class, Dedicated fixed amortized cost, and crossover points.
[11:48] Priya: Please make the finance table show worst-case and best-case. we'll need to present to the CFO next week.
[12:05] Maya: Understood; we'll do conservative and aggressive scenarios. Priya, can you share the CFO meeting window?
[12:18] Priya: Thursday 3pm ET. If you can send materials by Wed EOD that works.
[12:36] Lena: about model quality — we can't accept any increase in hallucinations. how will the quantization pilot measure that?
[12:50] Diego: We'll create a short prompt set — clinical summaries, entity extraction — and measure precision/recall and manual QA. fail criteria will be defined with your MLOps.
[13:14] Samir: Who owns the QA? our team or Redwood?
[13:20] Noah: Joint ownership. Redwood will supply the harness and baseline metrics; Northpoint must provide the labeled dev examples for accurate comparison.
[13:40] Omar: Latency dashboards — can we get exported traces for our observability?
[13:50] Diego: Yes, we provide tracing hooks, per-token latency breakdowns, and export to your datadog/new relic via our tracing integration.
[14:10] Priya: what's included in the security brief you mentioned? SAML, KMS, compliance certs?
[14:20] Maya: we'll attach SOC2 summary, ISO references, KMS integration docs, SAML screenshots, and audit log retention options.
[14:38] Lena: one more: rollout windows. we need canary periods during low traffic. can you recommend windows?
[14:52] Diego: Based on your peak, early mornings 0200-0500 ET are good canary windows; automatic rollback if anomalies exceed thresholds.
[15:15] Samir: okay let's confirm next steps and owners

[15:22] Maya: to recap — Maya will send cost forecast and Dedicated recommendation; Diego will deliver test harness and runbook; Lena will share traffic patterns; Priya will confirm CFO meeting slot; Noah will schedule technical deep dive for VPC/routing. any additions?
[15:46] Priya: timeline: materials by Wed EOD — that's 2026-03-11?
[15:55] Maya: correct, due Wed 2026-03-11. we'll aim for technical deep dive week of 2026-03-15. Diego, you good?
[16:08] Diego: yes. i'll draft an agenda for the deep dive and include latency benchmarks and KV-cache config.
[16:22] Lena: thanks, appreciate the quick turnaround. one ask: can you include dependence map for components that affect latency?
[16:31] Diego: will do — model size, batching, network hops, KV cache hits, and tokenization overhead.
[16:45] [Speaker 2]: (crosstalk) okay thanks everyone
[16:54] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up in email with attachments and next meeting invite. end of call.
